title: Farmers to protest in Brussels against EU budget cuts and trade deals

tea.why: Farmers oppose a proposed 15% nominal cut to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) budget and concerns over EU-Australia trade deal concessions.
tea.want: Protection of CAP funding, rejection of budget cuts, and safeguards against increased agricultural imports.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Organisers confirmed the march is set for Nov 26 to coincide with the EU leaders' summit on the 2028-2034 budget.

summary: European farmers are scheduled to march in Brussels on November 26, 2026, to protest proposed cuts to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in the EU's 2028-2034 budget. Organised by Copa-Cogeca with support from the Walloon Agricultural Federation (FWA) and other regional groups, the demonstration coincides with an extraordinary summit of EU leaders. Protesters argue that the current budget proposal would reduce agricultural funding by approximately 15% in nominal terms and shift financial decision-making to national capitals, threatening farm viability. Additionally, participants are voicing opposition to the EU-Australia free trade agreement, citing concerns over market access for sensitive sectors. While some agricultural organisations expect over 1,000 participants, authorities have not issued a formal response to the planned gathering, though potential traffic disruptions from tractors are anticipated.
demands: Protect sensitive sectors from trade deal imports
response: No official response reported in the sources.
